assumedContext: No primary filing retrievable; findings rest on the Q3 FY2026 earnings release, FY2025 results and trade press.

findings.claim: The backlog is a stock that depletes, not an annuity. EUR 162bn against roughly EUR 45bn of FY2026E revenue is about 3.6 years of work — shorter than GE Vernova's 5.8-year gas turbine queue, and the shorter queue is the weaker scarcity signal.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: The backlog is still growing faster than it converts. Q3 book-to-bill was approximately 1.57 (EUR 17.9bn of orders against EUR 11.4bn of revenue), and roughly EUR 26bn was added to backlog between Q2 and Q3.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Grid Technologies is the better asset inside the group and the backlog says so: a record EUR 51bn order backlog on transformer demand, and the tightest, longest-lived bottleneck of the three product lines.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: The gas turbine position is real but second to the grid business: the Siemens gas turbine backlog is approaching 70 GW, against GE Vernova's 116 GW.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Trade press on Siemens gas turbine backlog

findings.claim: The physical bottleneck is being relieved on a three-year clock, not a ten-year one. Siemens Energy's first US large power transformer plant, a USD 150m facility in Charlotte, begins production in early 2027; a further USD 185m, 550,000 sq ft plant in Jackson County, Georgia starts construction in November 2026 with roughly three years to full buildout.
findings.label: FACT
findings.source: Trade press on Siemens Energy US transformer capacity

findings.claim: The asset base is manufacturing capacity, not an irreplaceable resource. That is the structural difference from Constellation: a transformer plant takes about three years and a few hundred million dollars to build, and three firms are building them. A nuclear fleet cannot be built at any price on any relevant timescale.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the disclosed plant costs and build times

findings.claim: The genuinely scarce asset here is skilled labour and the grain-oriented electrical steel supply chain, not the buildings. The Georgia plant alone requires more than 1,400 new hires. Whether the industry can staff a 50% capacity expansion is a better question than whether it can fund one.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the announced hiring requirement

risks.text: The bottleneck can be relieved with three-year, few-hundred-million-dollar plants, and the whole industry is building them. This is a manufacturing constraint, not an irreplaceable asset.
The 3.6-year queue is shorter than GE Vernova's turbine queue and is being sustained by 1.57x book-to-bill. If order intake normalises the queue shortens quickly.
Backlog cancellation and repricing terms are undisclosed, so the durability of EUR 162bn is asserted rather than established.

catalysts.text: Industry lead-time surveys showing the first decline

conclusions: The backlog is a depleting stock of about 3.6 years of revenue — real, but a shorter queue than GE Vernova's 5.8-year turbine backlog.
It is still lengthening: Q3 book-to-bill of roughly 1.57x added about EUR 26bn in a single quarter.
Grid Technologies is the better business inside the group, with a record EUR 51bn backlog and the tighter, longer-lived bottleneck.

The decisive structural point: this bottleneck can be relieved. A transformer plant costs a few hundred million dollars and takes about three years, and Siemens, Hitachi and GE Vernova are all building them now. Constellation's nuclear fleet cannot be replicated at any price.
The binding constraint on the expansion is more likely skilled labour and electrical steel than capital — the Georgia plant alone needs 1,400 hires.
thesisImpact: Phase 2 confirms the backlog and dates the risk. The plants that relieve the shortage start producing in 2027 and reach full output around 2029-2030, which puts a specific horizon on the scarcity rent. The DCF in Phase 5 must fade the premium inside the explicit forecast window rather than carry it into the terminal value.
